captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a highly simplified, blocky character figure inspired by Minecraft's Steve. It is oriented upside-down for optimal 3D printing, standing on its flat, square head with its legs pointing vertically upwards. The legs terminate in blocky, forward-pointing feet, and the arms are angled outwards from the rectangular body, with one arm featuring a small rectangular slot. A thin, diagonal support strut connects the arms across the back of the figure to stabilize it during printing.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric, single-piece Minecraft Steve figure optimized for 3D printing by rendering it upside-down. The script should allow customization of the scale, head rotation angle, left and right arm angles, and leg angles, using blocky cube primitives for all body parts including the head, body, arms, and feet.
captions.factory: The model is constructed entirely out of parameterized cubes using the 'cube' primitive. It defines separate modules for the head, body, legs (with integrated feet), a tool-holding arm with a rectangular cutout, and a free arm. These parts are assembled within a 'drawSteve' module using 'translate' and 'rotate' transforms based on user-defined angles (hturn, langle, rangle, llangle, rlangle), and a 'supportarms' module adds a diagonal cube rotated at 45 degrees to act as a printable support strut.
